Green hydrogen has been hailed as the "fuel of the future", and since 2020 it has appeared in more than 60,000 media headlines, with 58 countries and regional blocs now having adopted hydrogen strategies - half of them in developing economies. The market, valued at USD 7.98 billion in 2024, could grow nearly eightfold by 2030.
 
But there are also central challenges yet to navigate. Land and water requirements are extremely demanding for reaching scale, and current costs remain high at USD 4.5–12 per kilogram, while dependence on critical minerals adds new risks. Without deliberate safeguards, the green hydrogen economy risks reinforcing historical extractive models, and exposing first mover nations to lost investments without the right guidance on technologies and pathways.
 
That’s why UNDP, together with the TIDE Centre, University of Oxford, published 📄 Navigating the Currents of Green Hydrogen: Towards a Human Development-Centred Framework, which I had the chance to co-write with Dr. Amir Lebdioui and Pavel Bilek,  🔗 https://lnkd.in/eEXrfn9t

The policy paper introduces a 3P Framework—People, Planet, Prosperity to ensure strategies deliver inclusive development:
🔹 People: Expand energy access, upskill the workforce, and support a just transition.
🔹 Planet: Safeguard land, water, biodiversity, and minerals through strong governance.
🔹 Prosperity: Integrate hydrogen into industrial policy, foster local value chains, and phase investments.
 
This report offers practical policy levers for countries to steer green hydrogen at the right speed, time, and direction. With transparent governance and context-specific strategies, it can become a driver of just transitions and shared prosperity.
